thread:
Nadia Chen: Quick onboarding PR question: my initial branch touches a formatter change + a tiny API change. Should I push the formatter across the repo first? worried about noise in review.
Omar Singh: avoid repo-wide formatter changes in your first PR. do a targeted change or propose a separate "formatting" PR and coordinate with the team.
Nadia Chen: ok. is there a preferred PR template?
Docs Bot: docs-bot: PR template located at .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. follow sections: Summary, Motivation, Testing, Rollout/Backward compatibility.
Mira Lopez: For starters, include a brief testing section with steps to verify locally. copy/paste is fine. Also add a line about whether this needs a migration.
Nadia Chen: thanks. local test speed is pretty slow for me  any tips?
Mira Lopez: enable test caching: export TEST_CACHE=1 and run `pytest -k <module>` for targeted tests. set `CI_LOCAL=true` to skip slower integration gates for local dev.
CI Bot: ci-bot: FYI - CI enforces a changelog entry for public API changes.
Nadia Chen: got it. what's the policy on updating package versions in PRs?
Omar Singh: bump only if necessary and open a separate PR for dependency upgrades. add CHANGELOG entry and mention security fixes if relevant.
Nadia Chen: will do. last: do we request multiple reviewers?
Mira Lopez: usually 1 primary + 1 optional for cross-area. small PRs can get by with just one. use the reviewers list in the README.
Nadia Chen: perfect, opening a focused PR now and will link the ticket. thanks!
